data.description:
## What is wrong

A plan-review run that reaches a verdict can lose that verdict entirely, and the reason given for the loss is false.

Under gate contention, `gate_status` returns a durable reason claiming the ticket store has diverged:

> the local ticket store has DIVERGED from the shared store — neither history contains the other, so this clone can neither see the shared state nor publish its own — refusing to decide the plan-review gate against a ticket store that is not current

Measured immediately afterwards, the store was in sync: `git rev-list --left-right --count HEAD...origin/tickets` returned `0	0`, with `HEAD` equal to `origin/tickets`.

This ticket is **not** about the congestion refusal itself. Refusing a run when gate slots are exhausted is correct and documented behaviour. The defect is what happens to runs that are *not* refused: they complete, produce a verdict, and then discard it.

## Evidence that no divergence occurred

"Neither history contains the other" requires a non-fast-forward. The tracker reflog across the whole affected window contains none — every movement of `origin/tickets` is either `update by push` or an explicit `fast-forward` fetch:

```
7e85fc356cc origin/tickets@{21:14:31}: update by push
6e33ae7db2a origin/tickets@{21:05:39}: update by push
4f4238a940e origin/tickets@{20:59:58}: update by push
417b602d2a4 origin/tickets@{20:59:36}: fetch ... --quiet: fast-forward
```

No force-update and no reset onto an unrelated history at any point. The precondition for the reported condition never held, so the message is a misreport rather than a description of the store.

## A candidate mechanism, not an established one

rebar's write path syncs by resetting onto the remote before committing, and the local reflog shows that reset interleaved with writes in the same window:

```
7e85fc356cc HEAD@{21:15:13}: reset: moving to origin/tickets
7e85fc356cc HEAD@{21:14:28}: commit: ticket: FILE_IMPACT adc7-2aba-2995-439a
6e33ae7db2a HEAD@{21:14:11}: reset: moving to origin/tickets
6e33ae7db2a HEAD@{21:05:35}: commit: ticket: EDIT 80a5-cbb1-ef06-4ba5
```

A gate sampling the store inside that window would see a `HEAD` matching neither its cached view nor the remote tip. Whether the divergence predicate actually misclassifies that state is unverified; the measurements above establish only that the reported divergence did not exist.

## Harm — a verdict that cannot be recovered

Three plan-review jobs were started within about seven seconds. All three were billed; none produced usable output:

| Ticket | `status` | `verdict` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `b505-d66e-86b3-4446` | passed | **PASS** | attestation never persisted; verdict unrecoverable |
| `2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9` | passed | BLOCK | `findings.reason: sidecar-not-emitted`; findings gone |
| `80a5-cbb1-ef06-4ba5` | failed | gate_congested | refused — expected behaviour, not part of this defect |

The b505 case is the serious one. A review that genuinely PASSED left nothing behind, and the documented recovery for precisely this situation does not work. `gate_status`'s own reason field instructs:

> Run `rebar sign-review b505…` if a review already PASSED but its attestation failed to persist

That command then fails, because signing needs a sidecar and none was written:

```
rebar sign-review weaponed-handheld-centipede
→ no REVIEW_RESULT sidecar found for this ticket
```

The error message therefore directs the caller to a command that cannot succeed in the state the message itself describes.

The 2041 case costs differently: `status: passed` with `verdict: BLOCK` and no readable sidecar tells the caller the plan was rejected but not why, forcing a second full billed pass to learn the findings.

## Why the false message matters on its own

The documented response to a genuinely diverged store is operator intervention through `rebar tracker-maintenance`. An agent that believes this message will either escalate an emergency that does not exist or begin repairing a store that was never broken. A misreport here is more expensive than a generic failure would be.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run that reaches a verdict writes its `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar even when the attestation cannot be persisted. Checked by: a test that fails attestation persistence and asserts the sidecar is readable afterwards.
- [ ] `rebar sign-review` can recover a PASS verdict from that sidecar. Checked by: the same test running `sign-review` and asserting the ticket ends certified.
- [ ] A run reporting `verdict: BLOCK` has readable findings. Checked by: a test asserting `findings.readable` is true for a BLOCK verdict.
- [ ] A store that is in sync is never reported as DIVERGED by the gate's divergence check. Checked by: a unit test over the predicate with a store positioned mid-sync, asserting it does not report divergence.
- [ ] Genuinely unrelated histories are still reported as DIVERGED. Checked by: a unit test over the predicate with two histories sharing no ancestor, asserting it does report divergence.
- [ ] When no sidecar exists, the reason text does not instruct the caller to run `sign-review`. Checked by: a test asserting the remediation text matches the recoverable state.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Provenance

Observed while driving epic `62dc-535b-5d05-421d`. Three plan reviews started within about seven seconds; all three lost. Store state verified in sync before and after by `rev-list --left-right --count` and by the full tracker reflog.
data.title: A plan review that reaches a verdict discards it under contention and blames a divergence that did not happen
